species.limit: 1 US bushel per person per day and 2 US bushels per boat per day
species.quote: Possession Limit: 1 US bushel per person per day and 2 US bushels per boat per day. Size Limit: 5-inch minimum carapace width (point to point). Females with egg mass (sponge) must be returned to water unharmed immediately.
species.notes: New for 2026–27: the 1 bushel/person, 2 bushels/boat limit and escape-vent requirement for pots (2⅜ in rings).

species.limit: No possession limit stated; claws only
species.quote: Size Limit: Claws must be 2 3/4-inch minimum forearm (propodus). Only crabs with 2 claws can have one removed. Only the larger of the 2 claws may be kept. No claw may be removed from a female with egg mass. It is unlawful to possess any stone crab body live or dead.
species.notes: Take one claw only (the larger) from crabs that have two, and return the crab alive.

species.quote: Possession Limit: 2 per person per day. Size Limit: 3-inch minimum carapace. Removal of tail at sea prohibited. No harvest of berried females.

species.notes: Federal Highly Migratory Species Permit with a Shark Endorsement are required in federal waters to recreationally fish for, retain, possess, or land sharks. All sharks must be landed with fins, head and tail naturally attached. Recreational anglers may only catch sharks using a rod & reel or handline. All other gears prohibited. Additionally, angers fishing recreationally for sharks are required to use non-offset, non-stainless steel circle hooks, except when fishing with flies or artificial lures.

species.notes: Shad & Herring page (https://www.eregulations.com/southcarolina/fishing/shad-herring-fishing-regulations): "HERRING One US bushel of herring per person per day. Herring Fishery closed in the Savannah River and in all rivers in the Winyah Bay River System (which means all waters of Winyah Bay east of a line running south from the southern tip of North Island to the eastern tip of Sand Island, and extending to the mouths of the Sampit, Great Pee Dee, and Waccamaw Rivers) except for the Great Pee Dee River." Nongame page: "American shad and herring may be harvested by skimbow net from February through April." and "Herring fishing is prohibited within one hundred feet of the fish lift exit channel located above the dam at St. Stephens Powerhouse."

species.size: No minimum; no more than 2 over 32 inches per day in Lakes Marion & Moultrie, upper Santee River, Pee Dee River (NC line to Hwy 301) and the Congaree & Wateree rivers
species.limit: 150 per person per day statewide; 25 per person per day in Lakes Marion & Moultrie, upper Santee River and the Pee Dee River from the NC line to the Hwy 301 bridge
species.quote: The daily bag limit for blue catfish harvest is 150 fish per day per person on all state waterways except the daily bag limit remains 25 fish per day for Lake Marion, Lake Moultrie, the section of the Pee Dee River from the state border with North Carolina south to the Highway 301 bridge, and the upper reach of the Santee River. It is also unlawful to possess more than two blue catfish greater than thirty-two inches in length in any one day in Lake Marion, Lake Moultrie, the upper reach of the Santee River, the section of the Pee Dee River from the state border with North Carolina south to the Highway 301 bridge, and the Congaree and Wateree rivers.
species.notes: Effective May 15, 2026 (Act No. 120) per the page's What's Changed box: "150 fish per person per day on most state waterways. Exception: 25/day for Lake Marion, Lake Moultrie, the Pee Dee River (NC border to Hwy 301 bridge), and the upper Santee River. No more than 2 blue catfish over 32 inches per day in Lake Marion, Lake Moultrie, upper Santee River, the Pee Dee exception area, and the Congaree and Wateree rivers." Freshwater limits page lists Blue Catfish as "See limits in Freshwater Nongame Fishing Regulations section."

species.quote: It is unlawful to take, harm, or kill grass carp or robust redhorse from public waters. Any grass carp or robust redhorse taken must be returned immediately to the water from which it was taken.
species.notes: Also on the Aquatic Invasive page: "It is unlawful to take, harm, or kill grass carp from public waters. Any grass carp taken must be returned immediately to the water from which it was taken. ... Sterile grass carp may only be sold, purchased or possessed under a SCDNR permit."

species.limit: Possession prohibited without a commercial permit
species.quote: Harvest and possession of horseshoe crabs is prohibited without a commercial permit. A permit is not required to possess a castoff or molted shell of a horseshoe crab.
species.notes: A permit is not required to possess a castoff or molted shell.

species.quote: Native freshwater mussels may not be taken without a permit from SCDNR. The non-native Asian clams, also known as Corbicula may be taken. Contact the Freshwater Fisheries Section at (803) 734-3891 for permits.
species.notes: Non-native Asian clams (Corbicula) may be taken.
